note: Hand-authored. Covers both multi-app's consumption of the memory engine and the engine's own internals (multi-graph-memory, a sibling repo at /root/multi-graph-memory, consumed as a local file: dependency) — the user chose to include engine internals rather than treat it as a black box, since the MCP scope mismatch (see below) is a real defect that spans both repos.

clientSide.statement: services/memoryService.ts is the client's only route to memory. Every function is bounded at 2s and answers null rather than throwing; the one awaited call is opening an episode, because a null episode id is what makes every later tap a no-op.
clientSide.correction: Relabeled from 'gate' 2026-09-06: services/memoryService.test.ts (added this session) covers the keepalive fix specifically, but not the full 2s-timeout/null-on-failure behavior this statement describes end to end — a partial, not a full, running check. See de-clutter-protocol-finder-of-truth.md / declarations-clarification-correction.md.
clientSide.hazard: Read the memory link from memoryRef.current, never builderState.memory — a handler closes over the render that created it, and a generation opens its episode during that handler. Already caused a real bug: a verified build failed to close its own episode, recorded 'abandoned' on the next reload.

serverSide.statement: One SHARED GraphMemory instance for the whole app, backed by .multi-memory/builder.db (workspace 'multi-app', project 'builder'). memory/bridge.js wraps it; memory/routes.js exposes /api/memory/*; memory/proposals.js is the declared table mapping validator issue codes to lessons — a code in neither PROPOSAL_TABLE nor NOT_A_LESSON is logged as an open question.
serverSide.correction: CORRECTED 2026-09-06, mid-fix-cycle: this entry originally said 'one GraphMemory instance per build id, backed by .multi-memory/<buildId>.db' — README.md's own prose, taken at face value during the original audit instead of reading memory/bridge.js's actual current source. That was already wrong: commit 6360b37 ('a lesson outlives the build that learned it', 2026-09-05) migrated bridge.js from one-store-per-build to this single shared store specifically because 'a lesson learned in one build was invisible to the next.' The 125 build-*.db files in .multi-memory/ are pre-migration leftovers nothing writes to anymore, not live parallel storage. This is the exact failure mode this audit exists to catch, caught against its own output — see de-clutter-protocol-finder-of-truth.md.

episodeLifecycle.statement: An episode is one generation attempt. It opens when generation starts and closes exactly once: verified (validator passed), failed (validator failed or the attempt threw), or abandoned (a reload/reset cut it short). The engine reuses an episode still open for the same objective rather than forking a second one, and any episode left open by a reload is closed at startup before anything can join it.

lessonLadder.statement: proposed -> qualified -> approved. proposed: something broke once and the table says what it teaches. qualified: tried in a LATER, DIFFERENT attempt, and that attempt passed. approved: a human said yes, only via POST /api/memory/lessons/:id/approve — reachable from no prompt or tool schema. The engine only ever puts qualified/approved lessons in its governed recall; a trial channel (bridge.trialBlock) additively injects up to 3 unproven, issue-matched proposals into the next attempt after a failure, in their own labelled block, recorded as applied so a pass is checkable rather than assumed.
lessonLadder.realState: As of this audit: 6 lessons total exist, ALL status=proposed. None have ever reached qualified or approved — see hetrodox-unconventional-approaches.json#lesson-ladder-never-climbed for why (not a ladder defect; a direct consequence of almost no episodes ever being recorded).

engineInternals.note: multi-graph-memory (/root/multi-graph-memory), version 0.2.0 in package.json. Verified directly against source for this audit, not recalled from a prior session's notes.

readOnlyMcpCore.statement: src/mcp/server.ts's ReadOnlyMcpServer is a hand-rolled, SDK-free, transport-agnostic dispatch core exposing READ_ONLY_TOOLS (fgm_read_memory_context, fgm_list_lessons, fgm_get_lesson, fgm_list_episodes, fgm_query_events, fgm_project_status). It has no mutation tools at all — not gated by a flag, simply never registered or dispatched, on the stated reasoning 'a flag can be set wrongly; an absent capability cannot.'

sdkAdapter.statement: src/mcp/sdkAdapter.ts is the one place the real @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is imported, wiring the SDK's low-level Server class's tools/list and tools/call to ReadOnlyMcpServer.handleRequest. The low-level Server is used deliberately over the newer, SDK-recommended McpServer, because McpServer.registerTool only accepts a Zod schema and READ_ONLY_TOOLS is already raw JSON Schema — converting would fork one source of truth into two hand-maintained copies.

stdioTransport.statement: bin/multi-memory-mcp.ts is the stdio entrypoint (B1): resolves scope via openMemory() -> loadConfig() -> the same config chain the multi-memory CLI uses, so an MCP client asking 'which project is this' gets the identical answer a CLI command from the same directory would. Registered in ~/.mcp.json as `node /root/multi-graph-memory/dist/bin/multi-memory-mcp.js` with cwd /root/multi-app.

httpTransport.statement: src/mcp/http.ts (B2) is a Streamable HTTP transport, Cloud-Run-shaped: X-Api-Key header (not Authorization: Bearer, which Cloud Run's own front door intercepts), stateless (sessionIdGenerator: undefined, since Cloud Run kills idle connections), /.well-known/* forced to 404 (so a spec-following client doesn't stall discovery before falling back to the configured API key), and the key check fails closed via a constant-time compare.

scopeResolutionAndTheRealDefect.statement: openMemory() resolves scope from /root/multi-app/.multi-memory.json — {"projectId": "builder", "workspace": "multi-app"} — the SAME single project-scoped store (builder.db) multi-app's own memory/bridge.js writes to (see serverSide.correction above — this was NOT always true, but is as of commit 6360b37). There is no ongoing structural addressing mismatch between where multi-app writes and where the MCP reads.
scopeResolutionAndTheRealDefect.correction: CORRECTED 2026-09-06: this entry originally described a live per-build-vs-project-scoped mismatch and proposed a buildId-scoped MCP fix on that basis. An implementer agent began that fix, was stopped mid-task once bridge.js's actual current source was read, cleanly reverted its changes, and confirmed (read-only) that multi-graph-memory's own SqliteStorageAdapter/GraphMemory write path is genuinely synchronous end-to-end (node:sqlite DatabaseSync, non-async methods, real transactions) — the engine cannot silently lose a write. That narrows the real defect to multi-app's own call sites.
scopeResolutionAndTheRealDefect.measuredImpact: builder.db was independently confirmed empty (0 events/episodes/lessons/evidence) via both the MCP tools and direct SQL, DESPITE already being bridge.js's correct, sole write target since 2026-09-05. The 6 real episodes found during the original audit live in the pre-migration legacy build-*.db files, not evidence of an ongoing split. See hetrodox-unconventional-approaches.json#memory-cannot-see-most-real-usage for the now-corrected root cause: client-side fire-and-forget fetch calls in services/memoryService.ts lacked `keepalive: true` (fixed 2026-09-06), and server-side memory.appendEventSafe() calls in server.js are unawaited before their response ends, vulnerable to a node --watch dev restart or process exit interrupting the async forBuild() step before the (synchronous, once reached) engine write runs.
scopeResolutionAndTheRealDefect.possibleFix: Client-side fixed: services/memoryService.ts's post() now sets keepalive:true (see services/memoryService.test.ts). Server-side: await memory.appendEventSafe(...) in server.js's builder/* route handlers before the response ends, rather than firing it unawaited — in progress as part of this fix cycle.

plannedUpgrade_localRagStack.statement: An on-device (Termux/llama.cpp) RAG stack — generator (qwen2.5-3b-instruct), reranker (bge-reranker-v2-m3), embedder (embeddinggemma-300m), classifier proxy — is running locally, intended to give the lesson ladder embedding-based semantic recall instead of the current rule/keyword-based lookup in memory/proposals.js.
plannedUpgrade_localRagStack.note: Nothing in either repo calls these ports yet. See models-adapters.json's localRagStack entry for the full component list. Worth sequencing AFTER the memory-blind-spot finding is addressed — a smarter recall mechanism built on top of a store that captures ~1% of real generation activity would inherit the same blind spot, just with better math on top of it.
